title: Dạ, chào ông
englishTitle: Respectful hello to an elderly man
summary: Different ways to say Dạ, chào ông in Vietnam show respect for an elderly man.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Dạ, chào ông is the respectful greeting for an elderly man or grandfather-age local. It is useful in homes, neighborhoods, markets, temples, family-run shops, and any moment where age respect is the main signal.

sections.title: The standard way
sections.body: Use it when ông clearly fits better than anh or chú.

phrases.english: Respectful hello to an elderly man

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: The phrase combines respect, greeting, and the elderly-man relationship word.

sections.title: Relationship swaps
sections.body: These forms move between elderly and middle-age relationship words.

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Use it when greeting an elderly man at a home, family business, market stall, neighborhood shop, temple, or local gathering.

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: Ông is respectful when the person is clearly elderly. For a not-elderly older man, chú or anh usually feels better.
